verdict: Added the chemistry the proposal asked for — sp3 ROTAMER sampling (discrete chi wells) and ELECTROSTATICS + INDUCTION — and measured each against SKEMPI, which gives a two-sided, honest result. (1) ROTAMER sampling is the RIGHT PHYSICS for the buried clash that minimisation alone could not solve last pass, and it is dramatic on the mechanism: letting a bulky mutant jump to its lowest-clash sp3 well turns impossible energies physical (e.g. 1TM1 I58->Trp goes from ~9e10 to -2.4 kcal/mol; 1JCK B23->Trp from ~5e8 to -1.8) and cuts the bulky-mutation explosion rate to 4% (vs 33% rigid single-rotamer, 8% soft-core, 3% flex). This is exactly what you need for an ABSOLUTE, usable energy. BUT — the honest catch, measured not assumed — as a standalone RANK predictor of measured ΔΔG on the bulky set, the RELIEVED best-rotamer score correlates WORSE (Spearman +0.13) than the RAW, un-relieved rigid clash magnitude (+0.35; soft-core +0.35, flex +0.10; best = rigid). The reason is real, not a bug: the raw rigid magnitude encodes 'how much steric burden this bigger residue imposes', which tracks destabilisation; once you relieve the clash to the best well, that variance is discarded and the residual energies compress. So the correct use is BOTH — rotamer-relieved energy as the physical absolute value, and the raw steric burden kept as a separate ranking feature. (2) ELECTROSTATICS/INDUCTION added real, held-out signal: the lost cross-interface Coulomb term alone correlates r -0.16 with measured ΔΔG(X->Ala) and the Debye induction term r -0.35; stacked on the held-out predictor the chemistry climbs r 0.48 (sterics) -> 0.52 (+elec/induction). (3) implicit DESOLVATION — an honest NEGATIVE result. The EEF1/Eisenberg occlusion desolvation term is physically real (burying a carbon is favourable, burying an unsatisfied polar/charged atom costs energy) but on THIS alanine-heavy validation it is a weak signal (r -0.18) that is largely REDUNDANT with the buried-contact count (both encode hydrophobic burial): adding it moved the alanine held-out r only +0.01 (0.52 -> 0.53), and on the larger 2602-mutation flex_vs_rosetta split it slightly HURT (0.528 -> 0.515). So the term is implemented and available but is NOT folded into the headline feature set — forcing in a partly-redundant weak feature just adds variance. A proper SASA / Poisson-Boltzmann solvation model (what FoldX/Rosetta use) might extract more, but our O(n) occlusion proxy does not on this data. HONEST LIMITS: rotamers are sampled on the canonical wells and selected by lowest steric energy (NOT Dunbrack probability-weighted, no partner repacking); charges are united-atom approximate. So this remains a fast TRIAGE force field speaking only to the near-field INTERFACE effect. Net: rotamer sampling fixed the buried-clash PHYSICS but not bulky-mutation RANKING (the raw clash magnitude still ranks better); electrostatics + induction gave the genuine held-out accuracy gain (research 0.37 -> 0.52); implicit desolvation, tested honestly, did NOT help on this validation and was left out of the headline.
